title: Kirby Problem 4.31
exact_target: Does every knot bound two orientable surfaces in the standard four-ball that are topologically but not smoothly isotopic relative to the boundary?
definition_tex:
\subsection{Definitions and mathematical statement}
Fix a smooth knot $K\subset S^3=\partial B^4$, meaning the image of
an embedding of a circle. A spanning surface is a compact connected
orientable smooth surface $F$ properly embedded in $B^4$ with
$F\cap\partial B^4=\partial F=K$. Proper smooth embedding includes
the standard collar condition at the boundary. Its genus is unrestricted.

Two such surfaces $F_0,F_1$ form an exotic pair relative to the
boundary if they are ambiently topologically isotopic fixing
$\partial B^4$ pointwise, but are not ambiently smoothly isotopic
under that same restriction. Explicitly, the topological condition is
a path $H_t\in\operatorname{Homeo}(B^4)$ with $H_0=\mathrm{id}$,
$H_t|_{S^3}=\mathrm{id}$ and $H_1(F_0)=F_1$; the corresponding
smooth family of diffeomorphisms must not exist.

Does every knot $K$ bound such an exotic pair? The surfaces may
have positive genus, and that genus may depend on the knot. The
question does not assert that every knot bounds exotic disks.
The topological isotopy ensures the two surfaces have the same genus
and the same boundary placement.

The universal quantifier includes the unknot as well as nontrivial
knots. Producing pairs for infinitely many knots does not by itself
establish the statement for an arbitrary fixed boundary knot. Both
surfaces lie in the standard smooth $4$-ball; changing the ambient
smooth structure is not part of the proposed construction.

\subsection{Short English statement}
Does every knot bound two orientable surfaces in the standard four-ball that are topologically but not smoothly isotopic relative to the boundary?
